findings.current: He made us promise, again and again, that even if he died, we would see the coup through.
findings.defect: The Korean says he earnestly and repeatedly urged them to ensure the coup succeeded; it does not say he made them promise.
findings.rationale: 신신당부하셨어 conveys an earnest, emphatic appeal, not an explicit demand for a promise.
findings.replacement: He repeatedly implored us to see the coup through, even if he died.

findings.defect: “Dull” changes the quality of the pain. 아릿한 describes a stinging or smarting ache.
findings.rationale: The source describes the pain as 아릿한, rather than dull.

findings.current: or one of the Ten Kings
findings.defect: The English specifies that only one of the Ten Kings might be included, while the Korean names 십왕 as a group without specifying a number.
findings.rationale: The glossary establishes 십왕 as “Ten Kings”; the source does not narrow the reinforcement to one member.

summary: The chapter is largely faithful, with a few small shifts in meaning and specificity.
